negative_reviews.author: S Kim
negative_reviews.text:
Disappointed Service.

I visited Meadowhall branch
at opening time on 24 September 2026. The restaurant was very quiet, with hardly any
customers.

The lunch menu was sitting at the front
where the staff kept the menus to bring out to customers, but we were only given the regular menu and nobody mentioned the lunch menu. When we asked about the lunch menu, the male staff member only then brought it over. He also seemed very indifferent and dismissive when we asked questions, which made us feel quite unwelcome.

When we paid, the staff member processed the payment without saying anything and simply walked away. There was no "all done",  "thank you" or even an indication that the payment was complete, so we didn't even realise we had finished paying and awkwardly left.

I've also visited one of London branches with my children. Despite being much busier, the staff there were much friendlier and more welcoming.

I initially sent this feedback by email to info@makiramen.com on the same day we visited, but received no response, so l've decided to share my experience here instead.

issues: Covers rose to 2,164, up 414 (23.65%) week on week as trade picked up after the summer holidays.
Spend per head fell by £1.70 to £19.85 (the report shows the percentage as +7.88%), as the Thursday student night took £5k but £5 ramen dragged spend down.
Sales were £43,802.66, up £4,986.62 (12.84%) week on week and £802.65 (1.87%) ahead of target, passing £40k again.
Labour was 21.96%, lifted by Thursday student night staffing and a queue almost to Wagamama all Saturday night.
Food and drink variance was good at just under 1%.
Deliveroo was weak, with one inaccurate order missing three items that could not be disputed.
Google reviews were eleven 5 star and one 1 star; the 1 star guest has been contacted and invited back for a complimentary lunch for two on Thursday.

A full time front of house job advert has been written and Hannah has been asked to make it live, with a trial shift early next week for a candidate with bar and FOH experience on a zero hours basis of around 30 hours over Christmas.
A front of house team member is taking about two months off for exams until 10/12, so a second part time or extra hire may be needed.
Dave is leaving in November, and Josh can take more hours over Christmas.
Compliance was 96%, but nightly WhatsApp handovers report 100%, so the GM will check them every night.
Michael's regional visit gave Meadowhall a marginal pass on cleanliness, while noting significant improvement in management and good efficiency.
Michael asked for louder music on Saturdays, more smiling staff and the five second rule of acknowledging guests waiting at the door even when busy.
Compliance at 100% and a week with no reviews below 4 or 5 stars are the stated goals, with the GM to post more review updates in the group chats.
At the BOH meeting all food reviews were 5 star.
A new induction hub arrived and works, but the requested pots never arrived, so Sophie approved buying another induction hub instead.
There is no hot water at the sushi hand-washing sink, and the water boiler behind the big fridge is to be checked.
Sophie criticised borrowing stock from Manchester; Artur confirmed a large order with Japan Food Corporation and said short notice promotions make advance ordering difficult.
Sophie noted food cost at 27% leaves room for proper stocking.
An experienced sushi candidate pulled out for the next two months; of five CVs only two had experience, so Artur will train an existing ramen team member to make sushi.
Region-wide (England): the £5 ramen offer is now limited to one per person through a backend change, announced by Amy Tang at the 06/10 KPI meeting.

Region-wide (England): the Mapal compliance app (transcribed as 'Maple') must be installed on site laptops and iPads, with photos sent to the management chat; front of house staff may no longer use personal phones for compliance on shift, while kitchen staff may use their own phones.

Region-wide (England): table toppers must carry exactly one drink menu, one XOXO drink and one ramen loyalty card, and marketing material requests go to the England group chat for Amy Tang to forward to marketing.

Region-wide (England): at the 06/10 BOH meeting Sophie asked sites to top up stock through the promotions rather than hold back for food cost limits, to monitor dashboard stock levels, and to stop borrowing stock between branches.

Region-wide (England, AM Updates 07/10): deep cleans have been completed at all sites, and Inka Cheung and Amy Tang are drawing up an action plan for FOH training days to re-establish hospitality standards.
Region-wide (England, AM Updates 07/10): the required menus are the lunch menu, orange, ramlo tea (as transcribed), XOXO drinks and the main drinks menu, and the Trip to Japan menu ends in November.
